title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up the boundary stratification of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification \hat M_{g,ν} (he writes 'MD' for Mumford–Deligne) of the moduli stack M_{g,ν} of smooth curves of genus g with ν marked points. For each isomorphism type [G] of 'MD-graph' (a stable dual graph: vertices α carrying genus g_α and marked points, edges for nodes) of numerical type (g,ν), the previous page defines the stack M_{[G]} of stable curves whose dual graph is of type [G]. Standard curves of type [G] are universal for such curves, which gives a morphism M_{[G]} → \hat M_{g,ν} that is an immersion (eq. 25).

This page:
(i) Trivial graph. For the trivial graph (one vertex of genus g carrying all ν marked points, no edges), the construction returns the canonical open immersion M_{g,ν} ↪ \hat M_{g,ν} (eq. 26). This is the open stratum of smooth curves.
(ii) Partition into strata. Identify each M_{[G]} with a locally closed substack ('sous-multiplicité') of \hat M_{g,ν}. As [G] runs over the finitely many stable graph types of type (g,ν), the M_{[G]} form a partition of \hat M_{g,ν} into finitely many locally closed strata. This is the stratification by topological type, or dual graph.
(iii) Remark on closures. The closure of a stratum M_{[G]} is a finite union of strata M_{[G']}. One says [G'] is a specialization of [G] if M_{[G']} lies in the closure of M_{[G]}.

The next page states that this is a partial order with a greatest element (the trivial graph). It announces that specialization will be made combinatorial via 'morphisms (générisations)' of MD-graphs, that is, edge contractions. It then computes the dimension of the stratum from the finite cover M_G ≅ ∏ M_{g_α, \hat I_α}.

The purpose is to describe the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}: the combinatorics of the boundary as input for the Teichmüller tower and Galois-action program.
errors: No mathematical errors. Minor point: the immersion M_{[G]} → \hat M_{g,ν} is a locally closed immersion of stacks, with M_{[G]} the quotient of ∏ M_{g_α,\hat I_α} by Aut(G). Grothendieck's 'immersion' is correct in that sense.
That the closure of a stratum is a union of strata (the frontier condition) is stated without proof. It is true and standard for the boundary stratification.

ideas.what: Closure of a stratum is a union of strata; specialization order on graph types, later to be described by graph 'générisations' (edge contractions)

ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Deligne–Mumford; graph-category formalism later in Getzler–Kapranov modular operads, 1998)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, correct exposition of the Deligne–Mumford boundary stratification by dual graphs. The page itself contains nothing that is absent from the literature. The announced 'morphisms (générisations)' of MD-graphs prefigure the stable-graph categories later used for modular operads. That idea is only foreshadowed on the next page, not developed here.
transcription_corrections: Equation number is (26), not (76); it follows (25) on the previous page.
'une réunion finie [-des-] {+de+}' — the text reads 'une réunion finie de(s) M_{[G']}', with an overwritten 'les'/'des'.
The final condition is best read as M_{[G']} ⊂ \overline{M_{[G]}} in \hat M_{g,ν}. Only the closure of M_G is barred; the bar over [G'] in the image is a stroke separating the lines.
'un revêtement fini' on the next page is a separate sentence. On this page 'sous-multiplicités' is correct: it is Grothendieck's term for substacks.
